evidence.currentDescription: Schmid compares divine silence with parental neglect, arguing that sporadic comfort during desperate suffering is more expected under indifferent naturalism than perfectly loving theism.
evidence.lockedProposition: A loving parent would comfort a desperately suffering child, whereas many sufferers experience only silence; this sporadic pattern is more expected on indifferent naturalism.

It seems to me that a good parent, we would expect them to offer that kind of comfort, to reassure the child that I'm here for you. I'm here with you. I love you. Things are going to turn out okay. So, it seems like we have some pretty strong evidence for naturalism over and against theism here. It's not decisive.
